title: 30 vs 144 Hz determinism checks are blind to frame-rate dependence (and cost 318 s)
detail: Both the Node test (tests/unit/sim/bots.test.ts:63) and the e2e drive bots that read the sim every tick, so input is tick-quantized and the log can't depend on frame rate whatever the loop does. Proof: a scratch loop that runs exactly ONE tick per frame regardless of dt (game 4.8x slower at 30 Hz: 97.4 s vs 20.3 s wall) still gives identical logs at 30 and 144 Hz for seeds 7/12345/42 (scratch det.test.ts, passed). SC1/exceptional #8 are therefore unproven by these tests; only loop.test.ts covers tick counts. The e2e also renders every one of ~14k frames for 6 runs, which is why it takes 318 s of an 11m48s verify. Fix: (a) assert wall time to result (frames*dt) equals result.tick/120 within one frame at both rates; (b) drive input through __lily.press at wall times on the common 166.67 ms grid (5 frames @30, 24 @144, 20 ticks) instead of bots, so the shell pending->tick path is exercised; (c) cut the browser run to one seed and draw only every Nth frame (CEO-approved hook option, e.g. frame(dt,n,{draw:false})) since Node already covers 200 seeds. Target < 30 s.

title: In-browser sim-step p95 budget check is vacuous (coarse timer reads 0)
detail: lastSimStepMs is a performance.now() delta around one ~µs step (shell.ts:257,266); Chromium's clamped timer returns 0, so p95 <= 0.25 always passes (WO-002 report: 'lastSimStepMs is 0.000'). It is reported as a budget check but cannot fail. Fix: time a batch (e.g. 1200 steps of a cloned run) inside page.evaluate and divide, or delete the check and cite the Node budget test as the only evidence.

title: Tap-on-pad during the 40 ms retarget window retargets the current hop to a different pad
detail: While squashing, sim.choices is empty, so tapCandidates() offers the layer AFTER the hop target and slotOf() maps a tapped k+2 pad via positionalSlot. If that tap is consumed within ticks(40)=5 of hop start, sim.ts:344 treats it as a retarget and redirects the CURRENT hop in layer k+1 (e.g. fast double-tap L-pad then R-pad ahead: frog veers right, possibly onto a soggy/curl or flanked pad). Conversely a tap on another pad in the target layer during that window isn't a candidate and falls to screen thirds. Fix: in tapCandidates, while frog.phase==='squash' && tick-hopTick<=retarget ticks, return the target layer's pads (from the takeoff pad) so the tap retargets to the pad actually tapped; only offer the layer after the target once retarget is closed.

title: Flanked X chip vanishes during squash but a retarget can still land on the armed flank
detail: startHop -> refreshChoices sets choices=[] and resets the flanked pad to idle, yet handlePress (sim.ts:344-351) lets a different key within 5 ticks retarget onto the armed flank pad, which is then judged eaten at land (sim.ts:261). The deadly pad loses its tell for the exact window in which it can still be chosen. Fix: in refreshChoices keep an armed flank pad 'flanked' while the frog is in squash, or make retarget refuse an armed flank pad (treat as a dropped press).

title: Pause-button e2e silently passes if the button is missing
detail: if (await btn.count()) ... else console.log('note ...') was a pre-WO-003 crutch; the button now exists (ui.ts:74 data-test=pause) so the branch is dead, but a renamed selector would turn the check into a note. Fix: check(await btn.count() === 1, 'pause button present') and drop the else.

title: Small per-frame allocations in the frame path
detail: view() builds a new ViewState every render; renderer.ts:690 (isChoice) and :862 (particles callback) allocate closures per frame; input.ts:196 allocates a PadMemory per connected gamepad per poll. Heap growth is within budget (look-perf +0.26 MB), so taste-level. Fix: reuse one mutable ViewState and PadMemory per slot; hoist the two closures to createRenderer scope reading a captured sim ref.

title: Title vellum reads as fog and creates ghost pads on the first frame
detail: Now: .ly-vellum is a flat rgba(243,235,216,.62) rectangle, 860 px wide on desktop (full width on mobile), 219-243 px tall. It has no shadow, cuts hard vertical edges through both banks at x=290/1150, and its torn bottom reads like a waterline. The pads under it turn pale, so the first frame shows a new 'ghost' pad look in a game about spotting look-alike pads. It also breaks the cut-paper rule (§5.2: hard ink shadow). Should be: remove the full-width sheet. Either (a) set the wordmark straight on the pond per §7.1 (ink, 3 px paper offset, plus a 4 px ink shadow at 38%), or (b) use a small opaque torn paper label (wordmark + 24 px padding, tilt -2°, 6 px hard ink shadow, like the cards) that covers no pad by more than 10%. Never tint the pads. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-01-title-t3000.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-01-title-t3000.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/w-01-title.jpg

title: Reachable pads are no brighter than the rest; the choice relies on 32 px chips alone
detail: Now: about 15 pads of the same green fill the screen, and the 2-3 reachable pads differ only by their ink chip (§5.2 requires reachable pads to be the brightest objects). An 'easy brain' player sees a carpet of pads, not 'these 3'. Should be: non-reachable pads drop to 80% value (or 15% ink multiply) and desaturate 20%, eased over 120 ms after landing. Reachable pads keep full value plus a 2 px paper rim at 40% alpha. Keep the tells intact under the dim (the shadow and notch must still separate in grayscale). Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-04-layer6.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-04-layer6.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-06-tau09-rt.jpg

title: Dragonflies rest on reachable pads, covering chips and tells
detail: Now: a dragonfly sits on the reachable → pad (layer 6), on the ↑ pad (tau 0.9) and on a reachable soggy ← pad (layer 35). Its dark ink body and wings overlap the chip and read as a mark on the pad, which looks like a tell. §5.4 says dragonflies rest only on non-reachable lilies. Should be: rest targets exclude reachable, flanked and trick pads, and wander paths keep r+6 wu clear of reachable pads while chips are shown. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-04-layer6.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-06-tau09-rt.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-11a-k34.jpg

title: Landing droplets land on the pad, not the water (polish 10)
detail: Now: the 6 paper droplets spawn and settle inside the pad disc around the frog and read as white dots on the leaf from +25 to +100 ms after landing. Should be: spawn at 1.0-1.1r and throw outward at 18-24 wu/s so they land at 1.25-1.6r on water, 220 ms ballistic, fading over the last 60 ms. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-02-hop-burst.jpg (frames +275..+350), bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-02c-buffered-burst.jpg

title: Danger vignette invisible at 375 px until tau ~0.9
detail: Now: the radial gradient starts at 0.5 of a w/2 x 0.62h ellipse, so on mobile only the outer ~90 px carry colour, peaking at alpha 0.21. Over teal water and dark pads it is not visible at tau 0.6, which leaves eye size alone carrying danger. Should be: inner stop 0.5 → 0.3 and alpha 0.35τ → 0.45τ with a floor of 0.10 once τ > 0.3, plus a 6 px solid jaw band on the bottom edge at the heartbeat peak. Recheck desktop, where the vignette already tints the side banks rust. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-06-tau-rt.jpg vs bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-06-tau09-rt.jpg

title: Desktop win frame is mostly empty sand, the card hides the route start, and the veil mutes the warmest frame
detail: Now: at 0.4x zoom the river is a ~250 px strip, so about 70% of the frame is tiled pebble texture. The route runs off the bottom edge and the start half sits under the card and stamp. From +480 ms the 30% ink veil turns the 'warmest frame' muddy brown, and the bloom burst is barely visible (~10 px petals). Should be: (1) zoom = (vh - 96) / routeHeight (route centred, full trace on screen); (2) on viewports ≥ 1024 px wide, dock the card on the right bank, 48 px clear of the river; (3) no ink veil on win; (4) bloom petals ≥ 2.5 wu with a 0.9 s life, drawn above the zoom. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-11-win-newbest.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-11-win-burst.jpg

title: Near-miss frame shows the jaws on the frog, so it reads as a bite
detail: Now: in the frozen 60 ms frame the gator snout overlaps the frog's legs and shadow with no visible gap. §6 says the jaws snap shut 0.3P behind the frog so the 'almost' is legible. Should be: during the clack, clamp the snout tip to at least 0.3P (7.8 wu, ≈29 px mobile and ≈47 px desktop) behind the frog's shadow centre, along the hop axis. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-08-nearmiss.jpg

title: Soggy's moving tell is too small to read at 375 px
detail: Now: the bubbles are r 1.2 wu ≈ 4.5 px paper dots on the rim, easy to miss at a glance. The tell a player actually reads is the missing notch, and the sunk card never names it. Should be: bubble r 1.2 → 1.8 wu (≈7 px mobile), rising 4 wu with a 1 px ink rim. Add a third callout, 'no notch', to the soggy diagram. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-04-layer6.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-10s-soggy-card.jpg

title: HUD round buttons have no hover state on desktop
detail: Now: hovering changes nothing, and my mouse-down capture did not show the 2 px press either (the :active rule exists). Should be: on hover (pointer: fine), lift 1 px with the shadow 2→3 px over 90 ms; keep :active at 2 px down and the shadow at 1 px. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-hud-hover.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-hud-pressed.jpg

title: Curl copy uses two vocabularies
detail: Now: the callouts say 'curled edge' and 'rocks', but the line under them says 'Folded edge. Rocking. Sneaky.' Should be: one set of words, e.g. 'Curled edge. Rocks. Sneaky.' (≤7 words, §9). Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-10c-curl-card.jpg

title: Timer tab covers the finish log; stale best stays under the frozen timer on win
detail: Now: the bloom-flowered finish log, the goal the player sprints for, sits behind the timer tab at k34. On win the HUD still reads 'best 10:00.00' while the card shows the new best. Should be: keep the log ≥ 24 px clear of the HUD's safe area (offset it +15% x or lower it under the tab), and update the HUD best on a new best (or hide it once the card is shown). Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-11a-k34.jpg, bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/d-11-win-newbest.jpg

title: Airborne legs read as thin stilts
detail: Now: at 1.3x scale the opened V legs are long, thin orange sticks about 1.4x the body length. Should be: leg length ×0.7, width ×1.4, with a webbed foot blob (r 1 wu) at each tip. Evidence: bureau/missions/M-0002-frog-chase/evidence/polish/m-02-hop-burst.jpg (+100..+200)

evidence: Both determinism tests now drive presses at wall time on a 166.67 ms grid (pending -> next tick; e2e via __lily.press, no bot) and assert sim time = wall time within one frame: tests/unit/sim/bots.test.ts 'determinism (F-001)' (200 seeds), tests/e2e/sim-determinism.e2e.mjs (seed 7, full river). Mutation proof: loop.ts forced to 1 tick/frame -> Node test FAIL, e2e 4 checks FAIL (30 Hz sunk vs 144 Hz won, lag 17425 ms); reverted (git diff src/loop.ts empty). Wall time 318 s -> 6.5 s in npm run verify.

Removed the vacuous lastSimStepMs p95 check from tests/e2e/sim-bots.e2e.mjs; header now cites the Node budget test (tests/unit/sim/bots.test.ts 'budget': full run <=150 ms, step p95 <=0.25 ms) as the only sim-step evidence. sim-bots e2e PASS.

sim.ts refreshChoices no longer resets 'flanked'; arming sets the pad flanked unconditionally; only clearFlank or an eaten-still lunge clears it. New test gator.test.ts 'F-004': armed pad stays flanked through squash+air while a retarget lands on it -> eaten cause flank; plus 'eaten standing still releases an armed flank pad'. npx vitest run tests/unit/sim: 47/47.
